extracted.intended_audience: aspiring authors seeking traditional publication with HarperCollins
extracted.subtask_description: Practical step-by-step guidance for preparing and submitting a manuscript (format, query letter, and submission route) to HarperCollins and its imprints. Focused on polishing, formatting, and following imprint-specific procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research specific genre and market trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Before diving into writing, research the specific genre and market trends. HarperCollins publishes a wide range of genres, so understand where your work fits and what they are currently interested in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit HarperCollins' website and explore the types of books they have published recently to get a clearer idea of their current interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure your work is original and polished
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your manuscript is original and polished before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare your manuscript thoroughly; originality and polish increase chances of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and proofreading
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing and proofreading are crucial steps before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take time to thoroughly edit and proofread the manuscript to eliminate errors and improve clarity and flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript formatting: spacing, margins, and font
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to proper formatting: manuscripts should typically be double-spaced with one-inch margins and use a standard font (e.g., Times New Roman or Arial) in 12-point size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow standard manuscript conventions (double-space your text, use one-inch margins, select a standard 12-pt font) to meet publisher expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a title page with contact information and word count
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your manuscript includes a title page that lists your contact information and the manuscript's word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear contact details and an accurate word count on the title page so editors can easily identify and assess the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft a concise, engaging query letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Your query letter is your first impression: it should be concise and engaging and capture the essence of your manuscript while highlighting your unique voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a hook that grabs attention, follow with a brief synopsis of the book, and include a short bio and any relevant writing credentials. A strong query letter can significantly increase your chances of getting noticed—take time to perfect it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check specific imprint guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission procedures vary by imprint; check each imprint's specific guidelines on the publisher's website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm whether the imprint accepts direct submissions or has particular formatting/packaging requirements before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether you need an agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Some HarperCollins imprints accept direct submissions while others require an agent; decide whether to pursue representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research imprint policies and weigh whether seeking an agent is necessary or advantageous for your submission route.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit according to given instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: When ready, submit your manuscript following the specific instructions provided by the imprint or publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated submission process carefully (method, materials requested, contact points) to avoid automatic rejection for procedural reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience and persistence; continue honing your craft
rubrics_metrics.description: The publishing process can be lengthy, so patience is key; continue to improve your writing while waiting for responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep writing new material, attend workshops, engage with other writers, and persist—continued effort and development increase long-term chances of success.
